L6418@P135: International flights from Australia,
L6419@P135: are steadily recovering from the impacts
L6420@P135: of COVID. In 2024–25 there were
L6421@P135: 209 thousand flights, up from only
L6422@P135: 45 thousand four years earlier.
L6423@P135: This chapter provides data on airline activity, aircraft numbers, on time performance and airfare
L6424@P135: price indexes. Information is provided for both international and domestic airlines, as well as a
L6425@P135: breakdown of airport traffic by state.

L6427@P135: Source: BITRE (2025), Aviation Statistics – Airport Traffic data
L6428@P135: Figure 12 shows Australia’s top 40 airports by domestic and international passenger
L6429@P135: movements. Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane are the airports which experienced the most
L6430@P135: activity, with some regional airports outside of the top 30 entering and exiting the list.

L6466@P136: Figure 13 shows international and domestic revenue passengers. Since the early 1980s,
L6467@P136: the number of fare-paying passengers, uplifted and discharged in Australia, was steadily
L6468@P136: increasing both domestically and internationally, before a sharp drop beginning in 2019–20
L6469@P136: and recovering to around pre-COVID levels by 2024–25.
